title: Stabilizer orbits and thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra
main_claim: The prime ideals of the Lubin–Tate ring E_0 that are invariant under an open subgroup of A_n^× are exactly 0, I_1, ..., I_n. The invariant radical ideals are those plus E_0. This settles Chai's Hope in the finite-residue-field form, at every p and n. Feeding it into the Barthel–Heard–Naumann support comparison gives the Hovey–Strickland conjecture: the dualizable K(n)-local category has exactly n+2 thick tensor ideals, and its Balmer spectrum is a chain of n+1 points.

issues.description: The claim that Homs between Banach–Colmez section sheaves are bundle Homs is cited from the proof of Le Bras Thm 7.1, and is stated for arbitrary additive (abelian-sheaf) morphisms with no Q_p-linearity hypothesis. That stronger form is asserted rather than checked. It is only ever applied to the Q_p-linear sheaf map nu_x and to Z_p-linear endomorphisms, so the weaker, standard statement is enough.
issues.evidence: The text reads: 'the proof of [LeBras18, Thm 7.1] establishes the degree-zero Ext comparison in the category of abelian sheaves on the big site... without an additional analytic-morphism or scalar-continuity hypothesis'. Prop. def:natural-comparison proves separately that nu_x is Q_p-linear.

coverage:
Read all six sections in full and checked each step in order.
- Frobenius separation lemma: subsequence argument, residue choice, and convergence for arbitrary k-linear lambda.
- Formal closure: the ideal I is radical and Hopf. The descent argument through D_m coordinates and the Krull intersection is valid.
- Reduced closed formal subgroups are smooth: the p-basis and Omega computation gives d=e.
- Annihilator lemma: sigma-stability of I, [p] finite flat of degree q^e, Dieudonne semisimplicity, p-torsion-freeness of Hom, and Tate reconstruction of the formal homomorphism.
- FF-curve nondegeneracy: degree argument for generic independence, and Delta_n⊗K_X ≅ M_n(K_X) used via the matrix-selection contradiction.
- Specialization map Theta_y: contraction estimates, explicit inverse, additivity, analyticity in y.
- Tate kernel is Z_p^r.
- Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism (Illusie/Lau torsor, determinant a unit) and height rigidity. Together these give an invertible differential for the Tate coordinates.
- Recursion lemma and integrality of the comparison series.
- Continuity of the stabilizer action (the [p]^N-kills-defect argument).
- Transport identity Theta_{y_g}(gz) = iota_g(Theta_x z). Derived Theta_{y_N}(z_i) = [p^N] Theta_{y_N}(dz_i), and hence U_N = s_N^{q^N}.
- Finite-jet lemma estimates and the q^N-root limsup step.
- Gross–Hopkins argument in characteristic 0.
- Auxiliary-curve and translation lemmas, the prime and radical classification, and the BHN support transfer and Balmer spectrum.

Consistency check: since nu_x is Q_p-linear, its kernel on C-points must contain the Q_p-span of T_x. I checked that alpha_x indeed kills the étale torsion of H_x(m_C), which matches a kernel bundle isomorphic to O^r. No contradiction.
sibling_notes: The family 311 board had no earlier entries when I read it, so there were no sibling results to compare against. Arithmetic core: formal closure plus Fargues–Fontaine nondegeneracy plus Tate coordinates. The spectral step depends only on the established BHN direction (Thm 4.9, Props 4.6–4.7), so no prime restriction applies.
